title: Anthropic Eyes Record IPO as Investors Bet on Near-Trillion Valuation
excerpt: The AI company behind Claude has filed a confidential S-1 and is meeting with investors ahead of a potential October listing that could value it at close to $1 trillion.
body:
• Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC on June 1, 2026, initiating the formal IPO process
  • The company was valued at $965 billion after a $65 billion Series H round in May, surpassing OpenAI as the most valuable private AI company
  • Banks including Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase are arranging investor meetings for a potential October listing
  • The IPO could put Anthropic on the public market ahead of rival OpenAI, which has pushed its listing target to 2027
  • IPO activity in 2026 has been the strongest since 2021, with listings raising $227.5 billion through mid-July

Confidential Filing Sets the Stage

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, filed a confidential S-1 registration document with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on June 1, 2026, according to The New York Times. The filing came just four days after the company closed a $65 billion Series H funding round that valued it at $965 billion — making Anthropic the most valuable private AI company in history, surpassing OpenAI for the first time.

https://x.com/crypto_banter/status/2087873848981049810

Banks leading the proposed listing — Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase — are now arranging meetings between Anthropic and potential investors in the coming weeks, according to Bloomberg reporting cited by TradingView. The targeted listing window is October 2026, though timing and details may still shift.

A Record-Breaking AI IPO Season

Anthropic's potential debut comes during what has become the most active IPO season in years. Listings have raised $227.5 billion in 2026 through mid-July, the strongest total since 2021, according to TradingView.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=AjJ0oiBqxjo

SpaceX set the pace with the largest IPO in history on June 12, pricing shares at $135 on the Nasdaq and raising approximately $75 billion at a $1.77 trillion valuation, according to MEXC. On its first trading day, SpaceX stock briefly surged to $225.64, pushing its market cap above $2.2 trillion before pulling back.

"The crucial aspect to watch in Anthropic's filing is not just its valuation or revenue, but the undisclosed gross margin."

— Harrison Rolfes, Senior Analyst, PitchBook

Beating OpenAI to Market

A fall listing would put Anthropic on the public market ahead of its primary rival. OpenAI filed its own confidential S-1 on May 22, 2026, originally targeting a September listing above $1 trillion, but has since pushed its timeline to 2027, according to Bloomberg reporting. Moving first could give Anthropic an edge in setting the narrative around AI company valuations.

Anthropic could also beat DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company that has been gaining market share and may submit an IPO filing as soon as this year, according to TradingView.

Revenue Growth and Risk Factors

Anthropic's revenue trajectory has been driven by strong enterprise adoption of its Claude AI models across finance, legal, and software development, according to Yellow.com. The company was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, including CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei, and has built its brand around safety-focused AI development.

Amazon and Google have both made multi-billion-dollar infrastructure investments in Anthropic in prior funding rounds, giving it an unusual dual-hyperscaler backer structure heading into its offering, according to Yellow.com.

However, the path to public markets carries risks. A near-$1 trillion valuation demands extraordinary revenue multiples, and Anthropic has not publicly disclosed annual recurring revenue or profitability figures — details that will only become available when the S-1 is made public. Investors may also weigh uncertainty around Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration, which briefly restricted foreign access to two of its leading models and was the target of an Anthropic lawsuit after the Defense Department declared the company posed a risk to the U.S. supply chain, according to TradingView.

What's Next

The confidential S-1 process allows Anthropic to negotiate with regulators and refine disclosures privately. The company does not need to reveal its financials until 15 days before a roadshow begins, according to Yellow.com. Analysts at tech-insider.org project the IPO will price between October 15 and November 15 at a fully diluted valuation between $1.10 trillion and $1.25 trillion, with a primary issuance size of $25 billion to $35 billion.

If those projections hold, it would rank among the largest technology IPOs ever attempted, approaching the debut valuations of Saudi Aramco and Meta at the time of their respective market entries.
